Net primary production is growth after the trees' own respiration. A negative total means the forest lost carbon over the decade: harvest and slash burning took out slightly more than growth put back.

The model

How CBM-CFS3 keeps the books

The Carbon Budget Model of the Canadian Forest Sector (CBM-CFS3) is the Canadian Forest Service's model of forest carbon, and the core of the system Canada uses to report forest emissions and removals in its national greenhouse gas inventory. It does not simulate photosynthesis. It reads merchantable volume from a yield curve, converts it to biomass with national volume-to-biomass equations, and every year moves carbon between 25 pools using turnover rates set for the ecozone and decay rates adjusted for its climate.

Harvest, fire and other events are disturbance matrices. In the year they happen, each one moves a fixed share of every pool to other pools, to the atmosphere, or out of the forest as wood, and resets the stand's age. Before the first year, a spin-up cycles each stand through its historical disturbance until the slow soil pools settle, then grows it to its inventory age.

1Seven input tables
sit_inventory.csv
sit_classifiers.csv
sit_yield.csv
sit_events.csv
sit_transitions.csv
sit_age_classes.csv
sit_disturbance_types.csv

Built from the inventory: one row per stand and species group, its growth curve, and the events that hit it. A mapping file ties them to CBM's default species, disturbance types and the Boreal Shield West spatial unit.

→ CSV tables + mapping.json
2Standard Import Tool
sit_helper.csv_import(
  csv_dir="sit_directory",
  imported_project_path=
    "sit_trial_stack1.mdb")

Checks the tables against each other and writes them into a CBM-CFS3 project, an Access database.

→ project database
3Makelist and simulation
projectsimulator.run(
  project_path=
    "sit_trial_stack1.mdb",
  results_database_path=
    "..._result.mdb",
  n_timesteps=30,
  skip_makelist=False)

Makelist turns each yield curve into biomass curves and builds the simulation list; CBM then spins every stand up and steps the inventory forward one year at a time.

→ results database, one per stack
4Read the results
cbm3_results.load_pool_indicators(
  results_path,
  classifier_set_grouping=True)

Pools, fluxes, stock changes and disturbed area come back from tables such as tblPoolIndicators and tblDistIndicators, for every stand and year. This page reads 2000 to 2010.

Forest by forest

What goes into each forest, and what comes out

A forest management unit is the area one licence holder plans harvest for under Ontario's forest management plans. Its Forest Resource Inventory maps every stand as a polygon with its species mix, age and any recorded harvest, fire or blowdown. Each forest stand becomes a CBM record; the results come back per stand, so they can be mapped the same way.

Forest management unit 130

Wabigoon

Method

From inventory polygons to carbon pools

The inventory is turned into the seven tables CBM-CFS3's Standard Import Tool reads, the model steps each forest forward one year at a time from 2000, and the pool and flux indicators are read back from the results databases for every stand. The runs continue past 2010, but the inventories record no harvest or fire after that, so this page stops at 2010. Each stage is a notebook on GitHub: preprocessing, running CBM-CFS3 and post-processing.

Growth curves

Two curves drive every stand

CBM grows biomass from merchantable volume by age. This analysis gives every softwood stand the same curve and every hardwood stand another, rather than curves by species and site class. Stand age decides where on the curve each stand starts in 2000.

Close-up

An inventory, polygon by polygon

Follow one 24 × 24 km window in Wabigoon Forest, picked because much of it was harvested after 2000. Thin lines are inventory polygon edges: 1,000 polygons, median forest stand 10 ha.

Leading species

Species set the growth curve

The leading species decides whether a stand grows on the softwood or the hardwood curve. Broadleaf here means aspen, poplar and birch.

Age in 2000

Age sets the starting point

Inventory age is moved back to 2000. Stands that originated after 2000 are started at 100 years and then reset by the disturbance that created them.

Disturbance events

Harvest and fire happen in their year

Each depletion recorded after 2000 becomes a CBM event in that year. Harvest is modelled as clear-cut with slash-burn and fire as wildfire; both reset the stand to age zero.

Biomass carbon, 2000

The model's starting stock

CBM spins each stand up to its age in 2000 and fills its biomass and dead organic matter pools.

Mean biomass carbon in the window: 40 t C/ha

Biomass carbon, 2010

Cut blocks empty out, the rest keeps growing

Harvested and burned stands drop to near zero biomass; their carbon leaves as wood products or emissions, or moves into deadwood and soil.

Mean biomass carbon: 40 t C/ha

Change, 2000–2010

Subtract the two years

Stands cut or burned in the decade lose nearly all their biomass carbon; the stands left standing each add a few tonnes per hectare.

Lost more than 20 t C/ha: 1,000 ha · untouched stands gained 3 t C/ha on average

Checks on the run

The books balance

Every number on this page was read straight from the CBM-CFS3 result databases. These checks confirm the runs hold together: area, carbon accounting, events and the per-stand extraction.

    Caveats

    Before quoting a number

    Keep in mind

    • Carbon is in tonnes of carbon (t C), not tonnes of biomass; biomass is roughly twice the carbon.
    • Results stop at 2010. The inventories record harvest and fire up to 2009 in Wabigoon and 2010 in Trout Lake, so later years of the runs carry growth and decay only and are left out.
    • Every stand uses one of two generic yield curves, so differences between species and site classes are not modelled.
    • The exported 2010 biomass product stores biomass carbon (t C/ha) under a Mg/ha label. Relabel it, or roughly double the values, before using it as dry biomass.
    • Blowdown, drought and flood map to CBM's "Unknown" disturbance type: they reset stand age but move no carbon in these runs.
    • Harvest is modelled as clear-cut with slash-burn, so every harvest also burns its slash; that burning is most of the disturbance emissions.
    • Stands that originated after 2000 start the run at 100 years old, then reset when their recorded disturbance happens.
    • A few Trout Lake stands share a shortened polygon ID; their carbon is averaged between them on the maps.

    Next steps

    • Replace the two generic yield curves with Ontario growth and yield curves by species and site class.
    • Add harvest and fire after 2010, from the annual reports or national satellite records, to carry the story forward.

    Model: Kurz, W.A. et al. (2009). CBM-CFS3: a model of carbon-dynamics in forestry and land-use change implementing IPCC standards. Ecological Modelling 220, 480–504. Runs driven with cbm3_python.
